Run 4 surrogate diagnostics

Run 4 improves substantially over run 3 on matched initial validation designs and finds better Finesse-verified PSO designs. Its best saved full cost is 0.0102834 at round 10, 39.3% lower than run 3's best. Signed-difference MAE on the same valid initial validation designs falls by 53.2%. However, the model still misses symmetric response shape, often understates sensitivity, and does not improve difference accuracy consistently with each feedback update. Low difference MAE alone is misleading when the true changes are very small.

This analysis uses saved Finesse labels, production checkpoints and captured online evaluations. Separate local experiments use diagnostic checkpoints. The notebook can be refreshed from these artifacts without training or optical power solves.

Data, features, and the actual intervention

The full run 4 audit contains 140 groups / 700 rows: 500 initial rows and 200 feedback rows. There are 118 valid fixed-q groups. The initial data has 78 valid groups and 22 invalid groups, 104 zero-power rows, and 230 rows in the saved 282.09 ± 0.01 W center band. All 40 feedback groups are valid fixed-q groups. Zero labels alone cannot identify instability or solver failure.

Run 3 and run 4 have identical parsed initial features and labels, initial design splits (80 training / 20 validation), normalization, architecture, and seed 9302. Both use 1,000 base epochs, batch size 32, 20 feedback epochs, and automatic newest-row weight 100. Matching these settings makes this comparison more controlled than run 2 versus run 3. Both manifests record a dirty working tree; byte-identical initial weights and execution determinism were not independently recorded.

Run 4 uses production nominal_delta supervision. It directly supervises nominal power and signed partner-minus-nominal differences. This also changes which rows receive the direct power criterion: partner rows reference their nominal design, rather than retaining the old direct power penalty on every partner label. It is a combined objective change, rather than simply adding one term to the old row loss. The fixed training-derived difference scale is approximately 8.9252 W, reused for feedback. Sub-0.1 W responses therefore have small quadratic loss contributions. Checkpoint selection still uses all-row validation power loss, without an explicit signed-difference selection term. Invalid-q training transitions remain in production training and in the scale calculation. Invalid-q partners contribute 27.34% of squared initial training differences; valid-only RMS is still 8.57323 W, so removing invalid groups alone would change this scale only modestly.

All 25 selected feature reconstructions from rounds 1, 10, 20, 30, and 40 passed the saved rtol=2e-4, atol=0.05 tolerances. These checks use beam tracing and support feature plumbing; they do not validate optical labels.

Evidence: full data audit, feature audit, training audit and provenance.

Matched initial validation improves, but remains imperfect

Both base models are evaluated on exactly the same 15 valid held-out designs (75 rows / 60 directional responses). These validation designs were excluded from weight updates but used for production checkpoint selection; this is not an independent test. The five invalid-q validation designs are excluded here and retained in the separate all-row production metrics. Only 10 directional labels exceed the 0.1 W sign threshold.

Base checkpoint Power MAE (W) ΔPower MAE (W) Perturbation-cost MAE (W/m) Significant signs correct
Run 3 base 7.12385 0.642019 0.23489 2/10
Run 4 base 6.25405 0.30074 0.110748 6/10

The error magnitudes and significant signs improve. The symmetric response problem remains: on these 15 designs, Finesse decreases in both ITM directions for 11 designs and both ETM directions for 13; the run 4 base model predicts zero both-decrease pairs for either mirror. Most initial true differences are tiny: only 52 of the 312 valid initial directional labels exceed 0.1 W. The baseline comparison below helps distinguish a small error average from learning those changes.

Production selected run 4 epoch 780 using the 20-design all-row validation power loss. Its recorded all-row power MAE is 4.74142 W and difference MAE 0.225926 W; those values use a different cohort from the valid-only table above. Loss values and selection criteria should not be compared as if the objectives were unchanged.

Accuracy on the same 40 run 4 feedback designs

All checkpoints below see the same saved geometries and labels. The final run 4 checkpoint has trained on all these feedback labels, so its result measures replay reconstruction. Earlier models did not train on these labels, but the geometries were selected adaptively by run 4's search.

Checkpoint Power MAE (W) ΔPower MAE (W) Perturbation-cost MAE (W/m) Significant signs correct
Run 3 base 2.13289 0.935642 0.273561 7/47
Run 3 round 40 6.76059 0.898612 0.258706 7/47
Run 4 base 4.87073 0.103184 0.00807261 9/47
Run 4 round 40 (replay) 1.18294 0.0934732 0.0178189 40/47

Run 4's base model is much better than run 3's on difference magnitudes at these points. Final replay improves nominal power and significant signs, yet its perturbation-cost MAE is higher than the run 4 base model's. In final replay, all 40 significant ETM+ signs are correct and all seven significant ETM− signs are wrong; neither ITM direction has a significant true difference in this cohort. Finesse decreases in both ETM directions for 32/40 feedback designs; the final checkpoint predicts 0/40 such pairs. The improved ETM+ signs therefore coexist with missing symmetric curvature. The search visits a region dominated by much smaller responses than run 3's trajectory. Final replay response shape.

Evaluation Model ΔPower MAE (W) Zero-response ΔPower MAE (W)
Run3 base / valid initial validation 0.642019 0.039697
Run4 base / valid initial validation 0.30074 0.039697
Run4 base / run4 feedback 0.103184 0.0725293
Run4 final / run4 feedback replay 0.0934732 0.0725293
Run4 original online 0.0723349 0.0725293

The baseline predicts ΔPower = 0 everywhere. Its error is mean absolute true ΔPower; it says nothing about nominal-power accuracy. These values show why the observed magnitude and sign improvements still do not establish an accurate local response model. Response baseline records. Both base checkpoints on valid initial validation and the final checkpoint on feedback replay have higher difference MAE than simply predicting zero response.

At round 40, replay through the final checkpoint gives:

Direction Finesse power (W) Final MLP power (W) Finesse ΔPower (W) Final MLP ΔPower (W)
nominal 282.014 283.069 0 0
ITM_plus 282.003 283.073 -0.0109718 0.00392821
ITM_minus 282.018 283.069 0.00407539 0.000541819
ETM_plus 281.751 283.063 -0.262587 -0.00582449
ETM_minus 281.899 283.072 -0.115191 0.00298002

The true perturbation cost is 0.031198 W/m, while final replay predicts about 0.00114383 W/m, approximately 27 times too small. Across the 40 matching feedback updates, nominal-power MAE changes 2.35016 → 2.2145 W, while signed-difference MAE changes 0.0723571 → 0.0731025 W. Individual updates therefore offer little average difference improvement.

Original online predictions are distinct from replay reconstructed from float32 saved features. Tiny rounded differences can change signs: original online has 32/47 significant signs correct, versus 30/47 in matching pre-update replay.

Evidence: checkpoint comparison, per-update feedback records.

The actual PSO outcome is substantially better

Costs use each saved full objective:

0.5 / nominal_power + 0.5 * sum(abs(ΔPower) / ROC_step).

Run Best true cost Mean true cost Last true cost Online nominal MAE (W) Online ΔPower MAE (W) Significant signs correct
Run 3 0.0169407 (round 4) 2.9962 4.77661 11.3952 9.92912 48/131
Run 4 0.0102834 (round 10) 0.0136565 0.0173719 2.35021 0.0723349 32/47

Run 4's mean true cost is about 219 times lower, and its best cost is 39.3% lower. Each run chose its own trajectory, so this measures the actual optimization outcome and cannot by itself isolate the loss change. All captured costs were reconstructed from original powers, exact ROC steps, and weights and checked against saved costs.

Run 4 searches ITM ROC −3169 to −2419 m and ETM ROC 3774 to 3868 m, away from the upper ITM bound repeatedly selected by run 3. Its best saved design (round 10) has nominal power 281.940 W at ITM ROC −2575.356 m / ETM ROC 3788.523 m. The original surrogate cost there is 0.00196104 versus true 0.0102834. At round 40, original online cost is 0.00225026 versus true 0.0173719 (about 7.72 times larger). The median true/predicted cost ratio remains about 6.08. Better verified designs coexist with systematic optimism about sensitivity.

All original PSO selections and cost components.

Controlled local fits and transfer limitations

The same local diagnostic as run 3 fits rounds 1, 10, 20, 30, and 40 (25 rows), one seed 9302, for up to 2,000 epochs. Loss variants within an initialization share initial weights, scaling and optimizer settings. The diagnostic paired objective is row log-power plus signed-difference supervision; it differs from production nominal_delta. Its difference scale is derived from the selected training set. Checkpoint monitoring uses training power MAE / power RMS plus difference MAE / floored difference RMS. These are local fitting tests, not a global replacement.

Initialization / scaling Diagnostic loss Selected epoch Power MAE (W) ΔPower MAE (W)
Fresh / local scaling center_focused 0 280.94 0.0700343
Fresh / local scaling log_smooth_l1 0 280.94 0.0700343
Fresh / local scaling paired 1850 4.17671 0.0147322
Round 40 / original scaling center_focused 0 1.25328 0.0946254
Round 40 / original scaling log_smooth_l1 0 1.25328 0.0946254
Round 40 / original scaling paired 1750 0.426908 0.015795

The row-power variants select epoch 0 for both initializations. The fresh initial model has extremely poor absolute powers but nearly flat differences; the combined score can favor it over later power fits because the true differences are tiny. Those rows describe retained initial checkpoints, not successful row-power training. Paired supervision improves both local power and difference accuracy.

Fresh diagnostic checkpoints were then evaluated without retraining on the other 35 feedback designs (175 rows):

Fresh diagnostic checkpoint Power MAE (W) Max power error (W) ΔPower MAE (W) Max ΔPower error (W)
Fresh row-power 280.921 281.234 0.0716717 0.401067
Fresh paired 8.43388 44.9436 0.236029 3.73229

Transfer groups remain correlated with the saved PSO collection policy. Good local or nearby-transfer scores do not establish coverage across the global search domain. Here the paired model's difference MAE increases from 0.0147 W on fitted groups to 0.236 W on transfer, with a 3.73 W maximum difference error. The retained row-power initial model stays almost flat and has roughly 281 W absolute-power error.

Evidence: fresh fit results, warm fit results, row-power transfer, paired transfer.

Interpretation and next experiment

The nominal/difference objective change is supported by better matched-validation metrics and markedly better Finesse-verified optimization results. Remaining evidence points to weak small-response supervision, missing symmetric curvature, and a mismatch between the training objective and power-only checkpoint selection. These mechanisms are plausible explanations, rather than independently isolated causes.

A useful next controlled experiment would preserve the complete initial split and global normalization, compare response scaling and a validation power/difference selection criterion, and report constant-response baselines alongside signed errors, sign counts and verified full costs. Validate on new whole designs spanning the search domain before interpreting nearby replay or local fits as global accuracy. Keep the best Finesse-verified design alongside the latest round.
